newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS revises British Columbia outlook to negative.
newsitem.headline: CBRS revises British Columbia outlook to negative.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service on Friday confirmed the long term debt rating of the Province of British Columbia at AA+ while revising its outlook to negative from stable.

The bond rating agency said it revised the long-term rating outlook based on the significant difference between the surpluses presented in the province's 1995 and 1996 budgets and deficits that may occur.

British Columbia had projected surpluses of C$114 million for 1995-96 and C$25 million for 1996-1997. Last summer, the province reversed course and announced a C$235 million budget deficit for 1995-96.
The British Columbia government said recently that it might also record a deficit for 1996-97.

Lower than expected economic growth, including labor income, retail sales, natural resource prices and exports were factors in lower revenues this year, CBRS said. A tax cut introduced in the 1996 budget also cut into the government's revenue stream.

To cope with the deficit, the provincial government is axing 3,500 government jobs, reducing spending and cutting subsidies to business. The moves are expected to save the province about C$750 million in the next 18 months.
While CBRS viewed the expenditure reductions positively, the bond rating agency expressed concern that the cuts would be sufficient to balance the budget in 1997-98.
Although British Columbia had relatively low debt levels, its economic growth rate was declining, which negatively affected government revenue, CBRS said.
